findings.title: CI stale-lock recovery can admit concurrent runs
findings.summary: On mkdir failure, ci-may.sh checks the PID. For a stale PID it prints that it is taking the lock back, but does not remove/recreate the lock directory or perform an atomic ownership claim before starting jobs. Two callers observing the stale PID can both proceed. They share .ci-may log filenames and ci_may_test/ci_may_db resource names, so overlapping invocations can corrupt each other's run evidence or job state.
findings.trigger: A leftover scripts' common Git-directory lock has a dead PID and two CI invocations reach the stale-lock branch before either replaces the PID.

evidence.detail: Dead-PID branch only echoes; proceeds to write into existing lock directory, without atomic stale-lock replacement.
Default database/container identities are shared across runs.

validation.result: Race path follows from the stale-lock branch and shared destinations; not executed or reproduced.
validation.limitations: No CI or concurrency simulation was run; timing and operational frequency are unknown.

findings.recommendation: Recover stale locks with an atomic claim protocol (for example, rename/remove under a guarded ownership scheme) and ensure only the owner removes the lock; alternatively fail closed and require explicit cleanup.
findings.acceptance: A disposable repo test with a dead-PID lock and two concurrent invocations proves only one obtains the gate; the owner alone releases it, and shared logs/containers are not concurrently written.

findings.title: Frontend CI omits the Excel export unit test
findings.summary: The dashboard CI invokes a fixed set of named test groups. src/dashboard/lib/xuat-bang-excel.test.mts is present but is not referenced by a package test script or by the CI group list, so this test does not run in the documented CI command.
findings.trigger: A change to the Excel export utility is reviewed using only the documented ci-may.sh gate.

evidence.detail: Frontend tests are selected by a finite explicit loop.
An actual test file exists for the export utility.

validation.result: The file is absent from the explicit CI list and package scripts.
validation.limitations: No frontend tests were run; this establishes selection omission, not a product bug or a previously observed false-green build.

findings.recommendation: Add this file to a named CI test group or make the CI test command discover all intended `*.test.mts` files.
findings.acceptance: CI command selection includes xuat-bang-excel.test.mts and a deliberate failure in that test fails the frontend job.

duplicate_excluded.reason: Exact same finding: status check uses --untracked-files=no and status publication attaches to HEAD. Do not create a duplicate candidate.

limitations: No test, hook, CI, build, database, production, secret, or PHI access.
